m.s: Rinse {rice} until the water runs clear. Put it in a saucepan with 1½ times its volume of cold water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes. Rest off the heat for 10 minutes with the lid on, then stir through {ricevinegar} and a pinch of sugar.
In a small bowl mix {soy}, {mirin}, {honey} and finely grated {ginger}.
Cook {edamame} in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain. Thinly slice {cucumber}, {avocado} and {springonion}. Stir {sriracha} into {mayo}.

Pat {salmon} really dry with paper towel and season the skin with salt. Heat a drizzle of oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon skin side down for 4 minutes, pressing it flat for the first 30 seconds, until the skin is crispy. Flip and cook for 2 minutes more.
Turn the heat down to low and pour in the glaze. Let it bubble for 1 minute, spooning it over the fish until sticky. The salmon should still be a little pink in the middle.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the salmon, edamame, cucumber and avocado. Drizzle with the sriracha mayo and finish with the spring onion and {sesameseeds}.

l: Flake the salmon over the rice and pack the avo and mayo separately. Eat cold or barely warm. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
g: Tamari instead of soy in the glaze, cooked in a separate pan. Mirin is usually GF but check it.
